mainEntity.name: How long does composite bonding last on eroded teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding typically lasts 5-10 years with proper care, though duration varies based on the extent of erosion, location of restoration, and patient factors such as diet and oral habits. Regular dental check-ups help monitor the restoration and determine when maintenance or replacement may be needed.

mainEntity.name: Can composite bonding stop further erosion?

acceptedAnswer.text: While composite bonding provides a protective barrier over treated areas, it cannot prevent erosion on other tooth surfaces or new erosion if underlying causes aren't addressed. Comprehensive prevention strategies including dietary changes and management of acid reflux are essential for protecting both natural teeth and restorations.

mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding painful for eroded teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: The bonding procedure is typically comfortable, often requiring no anaesthetic as minimal tooth preparation is needed. Many patients experience reduced sensitivity immediately after treatment as the composite seals exposed dentine. Any post-treatment sensitivity usually resolves within a few days.

mainEntity.name: What are the alternatives to composite bonding for severe erosion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Severely eroded teeth may require crowns, veneers, or inlays/onlays depending on the extent of damage. These treatments provide more comprehensive coverage and strength for extensively damaged teeth. Your dentist will recommend the most appropriate option based on individual clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: How should I care for composite bonding after treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maintain excellent oral hygiene with gentle brushing and regular flossing. Avoid hard foods, ice, and using teeth as tools. Limit acidic foods and drinks, and consider using a mouth guard if you grind your teeth. Regular dental check-ups ensure early detection of any issues with the restoration.

mainEntity.name: Can I whiten my teeth if I have composite bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite material doesn't respond to whitening treatments, so existing bonding may not match newly whitened natural teeth. If you're considering whitening, discuss timing with your dentist as bonding can be colour-matched to whitened teeth if performed after whitening treatment.
